summary: Add customer_note column, backfill existing rows, deploy new version with state-only migration while both versions serve traffic synchronized by a row-level trigger, retire old version, then drop the note column and trigger.
write_consistency: A PostgreSQL AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger sync_note_customer copies the written value from the column being written (note or customer_note) to the other column using DISTINCT comparisons, ensuring that whichever app version writes to its known column the other column is updated accordingly; reads from either version always see the most recently written value.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed because the trigger function had IS NOT NULL guards that prevented propagation of NULL writes, leaving stale seed data and causing column mismatches. This revised plan removes those guards, uses DISTINCT to only act on actual column changes, and adds explicit INSERT vs UPDATE handling to reliably sync values during concurrent operation.

stages.description: Add customer_note column and create sync trigger function and trigger.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_trig AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer();

stages.description: Backfill customer_note from note for all existing rows.
Deploy new version with state-only migration; both versions now serve traffic with synchronized columns via trigger.
Retire the old version; the new version continues running.
Drop the sync trigger and the note column.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
